passages.text: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!” But it proved to be futile.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.  
King Solomon was wise and powerful.  
He spoke to himself.  
He said, “Come now.  
I will test you with pleasure.  
Enjoy what is good.”  
But pleasure was empty.  
It was useless.  
It did not satisfy.
passages.original: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י לְכָה־ נָּ֛א אֲנַסְּכָ֛ה בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּרְאֵ֣ה בְט֑וֹב וְהִנֵּ֥ה גַם־ ה֖וּא הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.  
King Solomon is wise.  
King Solomon seeks meaning in life.  
King Solomon examines laughter.  
King Solomon says, "Laughter is foolish."  
King Solomon examines pleasure.  
King Solomon asks, "What does pleasure achieve?"
passages.original: לִשְׂח֖וֹק אָמַ֣רְתִּי מְהוֹלָ֑ל וּלְשִׂמְחָ֖ה מַה־ זֹּ֥ה עֹשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.  
King Solomon was wise.  
King Solomon wanted to understand what is good for people to do in life.  
He decided to test himself.  
He tried to cheer his body with wine.  
He chose to embrace foolishness.  
He let his heart guide him with wisdom at the same time.  
He did this to see what is truly worthwhile for people.  
He wanted to know what people should do under heaven.  
He knew that people live only a few days.  
He searched for meaning during the short time of life.
passages.original: תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י לִמְשׁ֥וֹךְ בַּיַּ֖יִן אֶת־ בְּשָׂרִ֑י וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ וְלֶאֱחֹ֣ז בְּסִכְל֔וּת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר־ אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי־ זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשׂוּ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.  
King Solomon expanded his pursuits.  
He built houses for himself.  
He planted vineyards for himself.
passages.original: הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י בָּנִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בָּתִּ֔ים נָטַ֥עְתִּי לִ֖י כְּרָמִֽים׃

passages.text: I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.  
King Solomon was wise and powerful.  
King Solomon made gardens for himself.  
King Solomon made parks for himself.  
He planted every kind of fruit tree in them.
passages.original: עָשִׂ֣יתִי לִ֔י גַּנּ֖וֹת וּפַרְדֵּסִ֑ים וְנָטַ֥עְתִּי בָהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ץ כָּל־ פֶּֽרִי׃

passages.text: I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.
King Solomon was wise and wealthy.
King Solomon built reservoirs.
He used the reservoirs to water his groves.
His groves had flourishing trees.
passages.original: עָשִׂ֥יתִי לִ֖י בְּרֵכ֣וֹת מָ֑יִם לְהַשְׁק֣וֹת מֵהֶ֔ם יַ֖עַר צוֹמֵ֥חַ עֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me, and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.
King Solomon was the king in Jerusalem.
He acquired many possessions and honors.
He acquired male servants.
He acquired female servants.
Servants were born in his house.
He owned many herds of cattle.
He owned many flocks of sheep.
He had more cattle and sheep than anyone before him in Jerusalem.
He accumulated silver for himself.
He accumulated gold for himself.
He gathered treasures from kings.
He gathered treasures from provinces.
He gathered male singers for himself.
He gathered female singers for himself.
He gathered many delights for himself.
He gathered many concubines for himself.
He enjoyed all the pleasures that people desire.
passages.original: קָנִ֙יתִי֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים וּשְׁפָח֔וֹת וּבְנֵי־ בַ֖יִת הָ֣יָה לִ֑י גַּ֣ם מִקְנֶה֩ בָקָ֨ר וָצֹ֤אן הַרְבֵּה֙ הָ֣יָה לִ֔י מִכֹּ֛ל שֶֽׁהָי֥וּ לְפָנַ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ כָּנַ֤סְתִּי לִי֙ גַּם־ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וּסְגֻלַּ֥ת מְלָכִ֖ים וְהַמְּדִינ֑וֹת עָשִׂ֨יתִי לִ֜י שָׁרִ֣ים וְשָׁר֗וֹת וְתַעֲנוּגֹ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם שִׁדָּ֥ה וְשִׁדּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.
passages.sermon:
I became greater than everyone who lived in Jerusalem before me.
I surpassed all who came before me in that city.
I kept my wisdom through it all.
My wisdom stayed with me.
passages.original: וְגָדַ֣לְתִּי וְהוֹסַ֔פְתִּי מִכֹּ֛ל שֶׁהָיָ֥ה לְפָנַ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אַ֥ף חָכְמָתִ֖י עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי׃

passages.text: Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.
passages.sermon:
I am the speaker in this passage.  
I did not deny myself anything my eyes desired.  
I did not refuse my heart any pleasure.  
My heart found joy in all my work.  
This joy was my reward for all my labor.
passages.original: וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁאֲל֣וּ עֵינַ֔י לֹ֥א אָצַ֖לְתִּי מֵהֶ֑ם לֹֽא־ מָנַ֨עְתִּי אֶת־ לִבִּ֜י מִכָּל־ שִׂמְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־ לִבִּ֤י שָׂמֵ֙חַ֙ מִכָּל־ עֲמָלִ֔י וְזֶֽה־ הָיָ֥ה חֶלְקִ֖י מִכָּל־ עֲמָלִֽי׃

passages.text: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
passages.sermon:
I looked at everything I had done.
I saw all the work my hands had accomplished.
I thought about all the effort I had put in.
I realized everything was meaningless.
It was like chasing the wind.
There was nothing to gain under the sun.
passages.original: וּפָנִ֣יתִֽי אֲנִ֗י בְּכָל־ מַעֲשַׂי֙ שֶֽׁעָשׂ֣וּ יָדַ֔י וּבֶֽעָמָ֖ל שֶׁעָמַ֣לְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֙בֶל֙ וּרְע֣וּת ר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֥ין יִתְר֖וֹן תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?
passages.sermon:
I turned my attention to wisdom.
I also looked at madness.
I also looked at folly.
I asked a question about the future.
I asked, “What can any person do after the king?”
The king has already done everything possible.
No one can do more than what has already been done.
passages.original: וּפָנִ֤יתִֽי אֲנִי֙ לִרְא֣וֹת חָכְמָ֔ה וְהוֹלֵל֖וֹת וְסִכְל֑וּת כִּ֣י׀ מֶ֣ה הָאָדָ֗ם שֶׁיָּבוֹא֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ כְּבָ֖ר עָשֽׂוּהוּ׃

passages.text: And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness: The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
passages.sermon:
I saw that wisdom is better than folly.
Wisdom is like light.
Folly is like darkness.
A wise person sees clearly.
A fool walks in darkness.
But I also learned something else.
The same fate happens to both the wise and the foolish.
passages.original: וְרָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי שֶׁיֵּ֥שׁ יִתְר֛וֹן לַֽחָכְמָ֖ה מִן־ הַסִּכְל֑וּת כִּֽיתְר֥וֹן הָא֖וֹר מִן־ הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃ הֶֽחָכָם֙ עֵינָ֣יו בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְהַכְּסִ֖יל בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ הוֹלֵ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי גַם־ אָ֔נִי שֶׁמִּקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד יִקְרֶ֥ה אֶת־ כֻּלָּֽם׃

passages.text: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?” And I said to myself that this too is futile.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a wise man.
He thought about his life.
He said to himself, “The same fate happens to the fool and to me.”
He asked himself, “Why did I try to become wise?”
He realized that being wise does not change his fate.
He said to himself, “This is also meaningless.”
passages.original: וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י כְּמִקְרֵ֤ה הַכְּסִיל֙ גַּם־ אֲנִ֣י יִקְרֵ֔נִי וְלָ֧מָּה חָכַ֛מְתִּי אֲנִ֖י אָ֣ז יוֹתֵ֑ר וְדִבַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י שֶׁגַּם־ זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!
passages.sermon:
A wise person and a foolish person both live in this world.
People do not remember the wise person forever.
People do not remember the foolish person forever.
In the future, everyone will forget both the wise and the foolish.
The wise person will die.
The foolish person will also die.
Both will die in the same way.
passages.original: כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין זִכְר֧וֹן לֶחָכָ֛ם עִֽם־ הַכְּסִ֖יל לְעוֹלָ֑ם בְּשֶׁכְּבָ֞ר הַיָּמִ֤ים הַבָּאִים֙ הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁכָּ֔ח וְאֵ֛יךְ יָמ֥וּת הֶחָכָ֖ם עִֽם־ הַכְּסִֽיל׃

passages.text: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a wise man who reflects on life.
He says, "I hated life."
He saw that the work done under the sun was painful to him.
He believed that everything is futile.
He saw that all effort is like chasing the wind.
passages.original: וְשָׂנֵ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־ הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים כִּ֣י רַ֤ע עָלַי֙ הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּֽי־ הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a man who has worked hard under the sun.
He hated all his work.
He knew he must leave his work to another man.
This other man will come after him.
The speaker will not keep what he has worked for.
passages.original: וְשָׂנֵ֤אתִֽי אֲנִי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ עֲמָלִ֔י שֶׁאֲנִ֥י עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ שֶׁ֣אַנִּיחֶ֔נּוּ לָאָדָ֖ם שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽי׃

passages.text: And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.
passages.sermon:
A man must leave his work to someone who comes after him.
No one knows if that person will be wise.
No one knows if that person will be foolish.
That person will rule over all my work.
I worked hard under the sun.
I used wisdom in my work.
This is also meaningless.
passages.original: וּמִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ הֶֽחָכָ֤ם יִהְיֶה֙ א֣וֹ סָכָ֔ל וְיִשְׁלַט֙ בְּכָל־ עֲמָלִ֔י שֶֽׁעָמַ֥לְתִּי וְשֶׁחָכַ֖מְתִּי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ גַּם־ זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a man who has worked hard under the sun.
He looked at all his work.
He felt despair in his heart.
He began to lose hope because of all his labor.
passages.original: וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֖י לְיַאֵ֣שׁ אֶת־ לִבִּ֑י עַ֚ל כָּל־ הֶ֣עָמָ֔ל שֶׁעָמַ֖לְתִּי תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.
passages.sermon:
A man may work hard.
He may use wisdom.
He may use knowledge.
He may use skill.
He may gain much from his work.
Another man may not work for it.
The first man must give his portion to the second man.
The second man did not labor for it.
This is futile.
This is a great evil.
passages.original: כִּי־ יֵ֣שׁ אָדָ֗ם שֶׁעֲמָל֛וֹ בְּחָכְמָ֥ה וּבְדַ֖עַת וּבְכִשְׁר֑וֹן וּלְאָדָ֞ם שֶׁלֹּ֤א עָֽמַל־ בּוֹ֙ יִתְּנֶ֣נּוּ חֶלְק֔וֹ גַּם־ זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרָעָ֥ה רַבָּֽה׃

passages.text: For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?
passages.sermon:
A man works hard under the sun.
He toils and strives with his heart.
What does he gain from all this effort?
He receives nothing lasting from his labor.
passages.original: כִּ֠י מֶֽה־ הֹוֶ֤ה לָֽאָדָם֙ בְּכָל־ עֲמָל֔וֹ וּבְרַעְי֖וֹן לִבּ֑וֹ שֶׁה֥וּא עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
passages.sermon:
A man works hard under the sun.
All his days are full of pain.
His work brings him anger and sorrow.
At night, his heart does not rest.
He cannot find peace, even in sleep.
This also is meaningless.
passages.original: כִּ֧י כָל־ יָמָ֣יו מַכְאֹבִ֗ים וָכַ֙עַס֙ עִנְיָנ֔וֹ גַּם־ בַּלַּ֖יְלָה לֹא־ שָׁכַ֣ב לִבּ֑וֹ גַּם־ זֶ֖ה הֶ֥בֶל הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
passages.sermon:
A man lives under the sun.
A man works and toils.
Nothing is better for a man than this:
He should eat.
He should drink.
He should enjoy the good in his work.
This ability comes from God.
I have seen this.
God gives this to man.
passages.original: אֵֽין־ ט֤וֹב בָּאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְהֶרְאָ֧ה אֶת־ נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ גַּם־ זֹה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי כִּ֛י מִיַּ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃

passages.text: For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?
passages.sermon:
God is the source of all provision and joy.
No one can eat without God.
No one can find enjoyment without God.
Apart from God, people cannot truly enjoy life.
passages.original: כִּ֣י מִ֥י יֹאכַ֛ל וּמִ֥י יָח֖וּשׁ ח֥וּץ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
God looks at every person.
God sees some people as pleasing to Him.
God gives wisdom to the person who pleases Him.
God gives knowledge to this person.
God gives joy to this person.
God sees some people as sinners.
God gives the sinner a different task.
God makes the sinner gather things.
God makes the sinner accumulate wealth.
God makes the sinner give what he gathers to the person who pleases God.
This is also meaningless.
This is like chasing the wind.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לְאָדָם֙ שֶׁטּ֣וֹב לְפָנָ֔יו נָתַ֛ן חָכְמָ֥ה וְדַ֖עַת וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וְלַחוֹטֶא֩ נָתַ֨ן עִנְיָ֜ן לֶאֱס֣וֹף וְלִכְנ֗וֹס לָתֵת֙ לְטוֹב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים גַּם־ זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
